problems: The almost fully exposed sun at x=1..13, y=1..11 sits above the cloud, with only a narrow, notched overlap around x=4..9, y=10..13. At 1x on the dark panel this reads as a gold head or ball resting on a white body, rather than a sun clearly peeking from behind the cloud. The badge preserves that stacked-object reading.

The overlap has several short dark steps between the disc and the cloud's left puff. At 4x/8x the joint is fussy, and at 1x those dark pixels visually detach the sun. This fails the requested clear sun-behind-cloud composition, although the shared cloud itself is correct.
icon-cloudy.fix: Keep the shared cloud drawing, palette and scale intact. Reposition the drawn sun farther behind its upper-left puff, approximately 3 native pixels lower, so a substantial lower portion of the disc is occluded. Resolve the visible overlap into one simple cloud contour instead of the current notched neck. Preserve the sun's upper-left highlight and the clear outer margin. Recheck the unlabeled 1x silhouette and the 2x badge: it must immediately read as partly cloudy.

problems: The two left trails at x=1..13, y=4..10 and y=13..19 merge directly into the flake around x=13..21, y=9..18. The result is one branching white mass. At 1x the flake loses its regular six-arm structure and reads as a clawed splat or small creature, rather than snow being driven sideways.

The right-hand forks around x=19..22, y=5..10 and y=14..19 have heavy hooked/blocky tips, while the upper-left trail contains alternating isolated-looking shade steps. The 4x/8x close-ups expose these irregularities; enlargement does not resolve them into a clean snowflake plus gusts.
icon-blizzard.fix: Redraw the flake and gust composition with a clearly legible, regular six-arm flake on the right and two simpler sweeping trails approaching from the left. Preserve visible negative space between the gusts and the flake's branches; do not turn its left arms into thick bent ribbons. Simplify the fork tips and interior shade clusters, retaining the white-blue ramp, one-pixel navy outline, top-left light and 20-22 pixel width. Select the version that reads as blowing snow at 1x, without relying on its label.

problems: The upper curled terminal at x=12..17, y=1..7, the large middle hook at x=16..22, y=7..14, and the lower fork at x=9..17, y=16..21 combine into a creature-like silhouette. At 1x/2x it suggests a running animal or scorpion ornament rather than dust blowing left to right. This directly fails the polish brief's non-weather-object rule.

The narrow connection at x=12..15, y=15..17 makes the lower band look like a leg attached to the middle body's underside. The nearly enclosed upper curl looks like a head, and the middle band's thick upright right end stops the left-to-right sweep. These are structural silhouette problems, not palette or alpha problems.
icon-sandstorm.fix: Redraw three broad, asymmetric tan/ochre dust bands with a clear horizontal sweep and open gaps between them. Remove the head-like upper terminal, the upright block at the middle band's right end and the neck joining the lower band. Use shallow, open curls with tapered ends instead of limb-like forks or closed loops. Keep the existing colour family, top-left highlights, one-pixel navy outline and full canvas presence. Compare unlabeled at 1x beside wind and blizzard; it must read as dense blowing dust before the weather name is shown.
